q: Calculate the expected numbers for a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.
Calculate the ratio of round to wrinkled seeds, ignoring colour.
Explain what question 2 shows about the shape gene.
On its own it gives about 3 : 1, the result of a monohybrid cross with a dominant allele, so it segregates normally whatever the colour gene does.
Explain why a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio is expected, using the gametes of the F1.

The F1 (RrYy) makes four gamete types (RY, Ry, rY, ry) in equal numbers, because the two chromosome pairs line up independently in metaphase I. Random fertilisation of 4 × 4 gametes gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Describe a result that would suggest the two genes are linked.
Too many parental types (round yellow and wrinkled green) and too few recombinants (round green, wrinkled yellow).

19.t: Working with data: a chi-squared test
q: Explain why each expected number is 40.
With unlinked genes a test cross gives 1 : 1 : 1 : 1; 160 / 4 = 40.
The critical value at p = 0.05 with 3 degrees of freedom is 7.81. State and explain your conclusion.
38.25 is greater than 7.81, so we reject the null hypothesis: the difference is too big to be due to chance.
Suggest an explanation for the results and identify the recombinant offspring.
The genes are linked on the same chromosome, with A and B on one chromatid and a and b on the other. The recombinants are Ab and aB (the small groups).
Calculate the percentage of recombinant offspring and explain how recombinants arise.
(22 + 19) / 160 × 100 = 26%. They come from crossing over between the two genes in prophase I, which swaps alleles between non-sister chromatids.
